newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani stocks end down on devaluation news.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani stocks end down on devaluation news.

text.p: Pakistani stocks ended down on Friday on selling pressure from foreign investors after Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz told parliament Thursday a marginal devaluation of the rupee was on the cards, dealers said.
The Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) 100-share index fell 12.03 points, or 0.75 percent, to 1,591.30. Losers led gainers 176 to 73. Volume fell to 34 million shares from Thursday's 57 million.

The devaluation news dampened the market sentiment that triggered selling pressure mainly from foreign investors, one dealer said. The market was likely to open lower after the Saturday-Sunday weekend.
"The outlook is slightly bearish and it would be appropriate to trade in holding stocks," dealer Zubair Ellahi of Kausar Abbas Bhayani Securities said.
PSO dropped 5.00 rupees to 267, Engro Chemical 1.00 to 152, PTCL 0.90 to 30.35, HUBCO 0.40 to 37.75, ICI 0.75 to 24.80 and Dewan Salman Fibre 0.55 to 39.45.
